subject: SS
title: Two lands become one kingdom
teach: The assigned reading credits Menes with uniting Upper and Lower Egypt around3100 BCE. Uniting means bringing the two regions under one ruler. Memphis became an early capital, or center of government.
The red crown stood for Lower Egypt; the white crown stood for Upper Egypt. The double crown joined those symbols. It is evidence of a claim to rule both regions.

Historians connect unification with Narmer, but the exact link between the names Narmer and Menes is debated. For a question asking what your assigned text says, use Menes. Do not treat a debated identity as certain.
A dynasty is a line of rulers from the same family. Dynasty tells you how rule passes through a family; it does not name one building or one job.
A pharaoh was Egypt’s ruler. The government collected resources, organized projects and defended the country. A united kingdom still needed people to carry out that work.
Keep three ideas separate: a ruler is one person; a dynasty is a family line of rulers; a kingdom is the territory and people under a ruler.

teach: BCE means Before the Common Era. For dates marked BCE, a larger year number is earlier. First learn the event order; do not guess from the order a textbook lists names.
